I ran `--review-pr` against `d1f57d81b...HEAD` (6 commits, 12 files). I generated the all-rules checklist (60 rules) to the scratchpad rather than the repo, so no tracked files changed, and considered every rule. I didn't need to look up any review learnings (no Level 1 or Level 2 zoom), and I made no code changes because this is a review.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-01/02/04, PR-01, NAME-01, REUSE-01, STYLE-01, TYPE-04/06, CONFIG-04/05, CACHE-02, TEST-01/06/08/09. The SPDX headers are all present, including on the newly touched `.yarnrc.yml` and `deployments.helper.spec.ts`.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | File:line | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Medium** (plausible) | CONFIG-04 / correctness | `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.ts:687`, `:696` | The PR adds `'1.5.0'` to `MULTICHAIN_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` (`:79`), but `checkVersionCompatibility` still checks the SafeToL2Setup and SafeToL2Migration conditions with a fixed `version: '1.4.1'`. For a 1.5.0 Safe, a chain that only has the 1.4.1 helpers could therefore pass (wrongly `MISSING_OWNERSHIP`), and a chain that only has 1.5.0 helpers could be wrongly rejected. Both new tests set `to` to `zeroAddress` (spec `:1727`, `:1783`), which skips this path entirely. Fix: pass `version` through, or map it to the right helper for 1.5.0 (1.5.0 uses `SafeMigration`), and add a test where `to` is not the zero address. I couldn't confirm the 1.5.0 helper entries in safe-deployments because `node_modules` isn't installed. |
| 2 | **Medium** | CHANGE-04 | `src/modules/transactions/routes/entities/settings-changes/settings-change.entity.ts:9`, `:15`; `src/modules/transactions/routes/mappers/common/transaction-info.mapper.ts:582` | This changes the external API. `setModuleGuard` transactions used to come back as `Custom`; they now come back as `SettingsChange` with two new enum values, `SET_MODULE_GUARD` and `DELETE_MODULE_GUARD`. The change is additive, but clients with an exhaustive switch on `settingsInfo.type` (web/mobile) need to handle the new values. Confirm the clients are ready or note it in the PR body. |
| 3 | **Medium** | CHANGE-02 / security | `.yarnrc.yml:17-19` | `npmPreapprovedPackages: '@safe-global/*'` lets the whole scope skip the 7-day `npmMinimalAgeGate` for good, not just this bump. It's a repo-wide supply-chain policy change inside a feature PR: a compromised `@safe-global` publish would install with no quarantine. Split it into its own PR with a justification, or scope it to `@safe-global/safe-deployments`. |
| 4 | Low | CONFIG-04 / TEST-01 (non-negotiable 6) | `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.spec.ts:1714-1715`, `:1723`, `:1770-1771`, `:1779` | The tests hardcode the 1.5.0 singleton, proxy factory and fallback-handler addresses (plus `as Address` casts), and these addresses exist in `safe-deployments`. Older tests do the same (`:1541`, `:1671`), but this adds more of it. Read them from `getSafeSingletonDeployment`/`getProxyFactoryDeployment`/`getCompatibilityFallbackHandlerDeployment({ version: '1.5.0' })` instead. |
| 5 | Low | TEST-06 / TEST-09 | `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.spec.ts:1752` | The `INCOMPATIBLE_SAFE` test depends on chain `1101` having no 1.5.0 deployments in the real safe-deployments data. The next bump that adds 1.5.0 there will break the test for a reason unrelated to the code. Mock the deployment lookups, or assert the condition up front so the failure is obvious. |
| 6 | Low | PR-01 / DRY | `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.spec.ts:1695-1805` | The two new tests are about 50 near-identical lines each (API mock, 1.5.0 creation-tx rewrite, chain mock); only the chain ID and expected status differ. Pull out a local helper or use `it.each`. |
| 7 | Low | CACHE-02 | `src/modules/safe-shield/recipient-analysis/recipient-analysis.service.ts:163` | Recipient/bridge results are cached. Results already cached for 1.5.0 Safes (the old verdict) will be served until `expirationTimeInSeconds.default` expires. The TTL bounds this, but it's worth a note in the PR, or bump the cache key if the stale verdict matters. |
| 8 | Nit | REUSE-01 | `src/modules/transactions/routes/mappers/common/settings-change.mapper.spec.ts:292` | The zero address is written out as a literal; use viem's `zeroAddress`, which the other spec in this PR already imports. The existing `DeleteGuard` test at `:255` has the same literal. |
| 9 | Nit | TEST-08 | `src/modules/transactions/routes/mappers/common/settings-change.mapper.spec.ts:308-312` | This test only checks that a static array contains a string. The classification that matters is already covered by the `SetModuleGuard`/`DeleteModuleGuard` tests. A test through `transaction-info.mapper` that shows a `setModuleGuard` tx comes back as `SettingsChange` would actually cover finding 2. |
| 10 | Nit | NAME-01 | `src/modules/transactions/routes/mappers/common/settings-change.mapper.ts:191` | `handleGuardLike` is a vague name; `mapGuardSetting` or `handleGuardAddressSetting` would say what it does. The generic helper itself is justified, since it has two callers. |

No other rule failed.

**Open questions:**
- Finding 1 needs someone to confirm which SafeToL2Setup and migration deployment versions 1.5.0 Safes use.
- Finding 3 needs a security-policy decision.
